items.title: FPL GW12 DEADLINE STREAM 🌍 FINAL TEAM 🔒
items.headline: DCL Leads a Split Gameweek 12 Captaincy Call as Raya Fitness Gamble Holds Firm
items.summary:
Dominic Calvert-Lewin stands out as the preferred Gameweek 12 captain, with his home fixture offering the clearest route to a haul in an unusually divided captaincy week. Kaoru Mitoma, Jackson and Alexander Isak are viable alternatives, while a bold captaincy on a Leeds defender such as Jaka Bijol is also defensible because of strong clean-sheet and defensive-contribution potential. Isak is preferred to Jackson where budget allows, particularly with Everton missing James Tarkowski, but Calvert-Lewin remains the top one-week armband pick.

The key squad decision is to keep David Raya rather than spend a transfer on Antonin Kinsky or another replacement. Mikel Arteta says Raya is training and could be involved against Manchester City, while reports suggest he arrives and leaves Arsenal training with the main group. There remains a risk of a zero-point goalkeeper if Arteta is misleading or Raya suffers a setback, but using a precious transfer on a short-term backup is judged unnecessary. Kinsky is still a reasonable insurance purchase for managers with spare transfers, especially given Tottenham’s Sunderland and Ipswich fixtures in Gameweeks 23 and 24 when Arsenal face Manchester City and Liverpool.

Defensively, Gabriel is a longer-term target, but immediate sales are focused on players with poor minutes security. Riccardo Calafiori is a priority exit because Arsenal are expected to manage his starts during the congested schedule; Luka Vuskovic, Jarrad Branthwaite, Virgil van Dijk and Brighton options are preferred replacements. Vuskovic is particularly attractive for his clean-sheet odds, attacking upside and defensive-contribution potential, while Van Dijk is viewed as a possible season-long hold given Liverpool’s excellent fixture run.

Palmer remains frustrating after sustained underperformance, but selling him before Crystal Palace at home in Gameweek 13 is considered premature. Florian Wirtz is the leading replacement if funds and transfers permit, ahead of Dominik Szoboszlai, although Palmer’s Palace fixture makes the short-term gain marginal. A more patient route is to hold Palmer and Morgan Rogers for the next two rounds, then reassess ahead of Chelsea’s tougher run. Sharda is a major concern after four blanks and a benching, but is still not worth forcing out if the money is better used elsewhere. Managers with Joao Pedro should prioritise Calvert-Lewin, while Evanilson is a hold after scoring in six consecutive matches.

Erling Haaland is acceptable to bench at Arsenal, especially for managers seeking upside from well-placed alternatives such as Gibbs-White, Mitoma, Rogers or strong defenders. He has scored in each of his last four meetings with Arsenal, so selling him permanently is not endorsed; the better approach is to retain him for Hull at home in Gameweek 16 and use the Arsenal fixture as a selective benching opportunity. Bruno Fernandes is avoided this week after missing training through illness, despite his appeal for Gameweek 14 against Coventry.
key_points: Captain Calvert-Lewin if owned; Mitoma, Isak and Jackson are close alternatives in a highly split Gameweek 12 captaincy field.
Keep Raya and roll the transfer where possible, as Arteta confirms he is training, but accept the residual risk that he does not start against Manchester City.
Sell Calafiori before the congested schedule if possible, with Vuskovic, Van Dijk and Branthwaite among the preferred defensive replacements.
Hold Palmer through Crystal Palace at home in Gameweek 13 unless selling him is essential to fund a major upgrade such as Wirtz.
Prioritise Joao Pedro to Calvert-Lewin, but keep Evanilson after his six-match scoring streak.
Do not sell Haaland permanently for Isak; benching him at Arsenal is viable, but Hull at home in Gameweek 16 is a key reason to retain him.
Avoid bringing in or captaining Bruno Fernandes after Pochettino confirms he misses training with a virus.
Managers on a Gameweek 12 Free Hit should strongly consider Calvert-Lewin, Isak and Jorgen Strand Larsen, with Mateta suspended before Wolves host Hull.

items.headline: Calvert-Lewin gets the armband as Joao Pedro exit frees flexibility for Gameweek 12
items.summary:
Calvert-Lewin is the preferred Gameweek 12 transfer and captaincy pick, replacing the injured Joao Pedro. The appeal is Coventry at home, penalty duty and a cheap-forward structure that retains flexibility for later moves. Evanilson is also attractive, but Calvert-Lewin is favoured because doubling on Leeds and Bournemouth spreads risk better than committing to a Bournemouth triple-up, while the saving keeps routes open to future midfield upgrades.

David Raya remains a major uncertainty ahead of Arsenal’s match with Manchester City, with Mikel Arteta providing no definitive fitness update. The recommendation is not to sell Raya simply because he is flagged: Arsenal’s long-term defensive outlook remains strong and there is still a credible chance he starts. Managers with only one free transfer are advised to take the risk rather than spend it on a goalkeeper; those with two or more spare transfers can consider upgrading a non-playing deputy such as Bentley to Guglielmo Vicario/Kinsky-style cover, particularly if they want protection for Raya’s tougher fixtures later on.

The planned XI keeps Raya in goal, starts Van Hecke and benches Antonio Silva despite Silva’s strong DefCon form. Chelsea assets Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers are also retained and started, more through fixture context and lack of urgent alternatives than current form: Palmer has disappointed, but Crystal Palace at home in Gameweek 13 offers a final appealing short-term fixture. Florian Wirtz is the standout midfield purchase for managers able to make the move, while Bruno Fernandes is a possible Palmer replacement for Gameweek 14 if Manchester United’s Coventry fixture appeals; his illness is not considered a serious reason to bench or avoid him.

Maxim De Cuyper is viewed as one of the best defensive targets and a viable captaincy differential against Newcastle because of his clean-sheet potential and advanced role, possibly even at left wing. Vuskovic is another strong defensive buy, especially with Newcastle vulnerable at set pieces. Free Hit planning leans towards Gameweek 15, when the existing squad has too many players facing difficult fixtures, although Gameweeks 14 and 19 remain viable alternatives. Managers still holding Bench Boost are encouraged to use it soon only if they can field a genuinely strong four-player bench, rather than forcing a weak setup.
key_points: Transfer Joao Pedro to Calvert-Lewin and captain Calvert-Lewin against Coventry at home in Gameweek 12.
Keep David Raya if possible; do not sell him solely because of the injury flag, although a playing backup is reasonable with spare transfers.
Prioritise longer-term upgrades such as Palmer to Florian Wirtz or Bruno Fernandes ahead of spending a final transfer on a goalkeeper.
Maxim De Cuyper is a premium Gameweek 12 defensive target and an aggressive captaincy option because of his attacking role and Newcastle’s set-piece weakness.
Start Erling Haaland over Palmer or Rogers if choosing between them, but benching Haaland is acceptable only for managers fully backing Arsenal’s defence.
Antonio Silva is a strong DefCon option but is narrowly benched behind Palmer and Rogers in the final lineup.
Avoid buying Lewis Hall or James Justin unless the transfer is a luxury; Vuskovic and De Cuyper offer better immediate appeal.
Free Hit Gameweek 15 is preferred, with Gameweeks 14 and 19 also under consideration depending on squad shape.

items.title: 🚨 Raya "update" 🚨 Buy Kinsky? 😬 FPL Gameweek 12 Deadline Stream 🚀
items.headline: Kinsky replaces uncertain Raya as Calvert-Lewin gets the Gameweek 12 armband
items.summary:
The key Gameweek 12 dilemma is Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya, whose availability against Manchester City remains unclear after an apparent nerve issue. Mikel Arteta confirms Raya trains but offers no firm assurance, while outside reports suggest the problem is short term and he has a reasonable chance of starting. With four free transfers and no other playing goalkeeper, the safer move is to buy Tottenham’s Antonin Kinsky rather than risk a zero, even though it feels inefficient and Raya may yet play.

Kinsky is preferred as a second goalkeeper over Bart Verbruggen because he rotates well with Raya and does not block a potentially valuable Brighton outfield slot. Verbruggen is the stronger option if selling Raya outright, but Kinsky offers a cheaper route to cover this week and future difficult Arsenal fixtures. The downside is immediate regret if Raya starts, while Kinsky also creates a double Spurs-defence exposure alongside Van Hecke; nevertheless, the security of a playing keeper wins out.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the preferred captain for Gameweek 12, ahead of Nicolas Jackson, Alexander Isak, Morgan Gibbs-White and defenders such as Diper. Calvert-Lewin has the fixture, penalties and a strong combination of floor and ceiling, while Jackson carries some minutes risk and does not take penalties. Gibbs-White is an attractive differential captain against a weak Chelsea defence, and Diper is a viable high-floor defensive alternative for managers willing to captain a defender.

Erling Haaland and Cole Palmer are legitimate benching debates because Manchester City visit Arsenal and Palmer’s form has been poor, but both remain difficult to discard entirely. Haaland is still the safer start in most close calls because he is a nailed penalty taker with a record of returns against Arsenal, while Palmer’s penalties keep him ahead of many mid-priced midfielders despite Chelsea’s issues. Morgan Rogers is the more common bench candidate when choosing between Rogers, Palmer and Haaland, although Tavernier is also a credible start over Rogers on underlying numbers and Fulham’s relatively favourable fixture.

Looking ahead, Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz is the premium midfield target, with Dominik Szoboszlai the cheaper alternative. Wirtz has the stronger open-play threat and is rapidly rising in price, while Szoboszlai offers set pieces and possible penalties but carries slightly more perceived minutes risk. Bruno Fernandes remains worth considering despite missing training with illness; he is expected to play Brentford, but cautious managers can delay the move until Gameweek 14. Raya’s uncertainty and the quick Gameweek 13 turnaround make preserving flexibility more important than forcing luxury forward transfers such as Haaland to Calvert-Lewin.
key_points: Buy Antonin Kinsky as a second goalkeeper if Raya is your only keeper and you have spare free transfers; risk Raya rather than take a minus four for goalkeeper cover.
Captain Dominic Calvert-Lewin in Gameweek 12 for his fixture, penalties and expected minutes, with Jackson and Isak the main attacking alternatives.
Start Haaland in most decisions despite Arsenal away, but benching him is defensible only if the replacement is a strong attacker such as Gibbs-White, Tavernier or Calvert-Lewin.
Keep Palmer ahead of most bench options because of penalties, although his poor form means he is no longer an automatic captain or guaranteed starter in every squad.
Bench Rogers in many tight calls involving Palmer and Haaland, but Tavernier has a reasonable case to start over him due to stronger recent underlying numbers.
Target Florian Wirtz for Liverpool’s favourable upcoming run; Szoboszlai is an acceptable budget compromise if funds are needed elsewhere.
Bruno Fernandes misses training through illness but is still expected to face Brentford; delay the transfer if you are unwilling to accept a late fitness risk.
Avoid taking hits for marginal forward upgrades such as Barry to Calvert-Lewin unless Calvert-Lewin is also your preferred captain.

items.title: RAYA INJURY UPDATE 🤕⚠️ | FPL GW12 INJURY + TEAM NEWS 🚨|  FPL Tips 2026/27
items.headline: David Raya fitness cloud makes a playing backup goalkeeper vital for Gameweek 12
items.summary:
Gameweek 12 begins a congested run of three deadlines in little more than a week, with goalkeeper selection a key concern. Arsenal give no definitive update on David Raya’s shoulder issue: Mikel Arteta says he is training, but offers little certainty over whether he is ready to start. Raya remains a hold rather than a sell because of Arsenal’s defensive appeal, but managers without a viable deputy are advised to use a transfer on a cheap playing goalkeeper. Kinski is one such route. Bukayo Saka, Oleksandr Zinchenko and Nuno Mendes remain out, while William Saliba is expected to receive some minutes this week.

Captaincy attention is on Alexander Isak for Newcastle’s trip to Brighton, despite Newcastle’s poor recent record on the south coast. Newcastle have few new concerns: Joelinton is definitely absent, Lewis Hall has trained after cramp and Tino Livramento is being assessed for a possible start. Brighton are without Kaoru Mitoma again, with his return still framed as one or two weeks away, while Matt O’Riley has an ankle problem after coming off at half-time in midweek. Diego Gomez was rested rather than injured, and several Brighton regulars have had minutes managed ahead of the league match.

Elsewhere, Bruno Fernandes is a late fitness concern for Manchester United against Brentford after missing training with a virus. A decision is due closer to the match, although he may still recover in time; Marcus Rashford is back on the grass but is unlikely to be ready, while Manuel Ugarte, Benjamin Sesko and Carlos Baleba remain out. Liverpool lose Cody Gakpo to a muscle injury for the Merseyside derby, and Everton are without suspended James Tarkowski for the first match of a three-game ban. Chelsea have Moises Caicedo available after a knock, but Joao Pedro, Reece James and others remain sidelined.

Illness is a notable late-week risk across several squads. Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi missed out with a virus and Antoine Semenyo is also unwell, although Bournemouth hope the latter is available. Sunderland report several players close to being affected by illness, while Tottenham have Bergvall ill and Savio is ruled out until after Christmas after a hamstring recurrence. Manchester City’s Semenyo is nearing a return and could be in contention around Gameweeks 13 or 14, rather than this weekend.
key_points: Hold David Raya if possible, but ensure a playing backup goalkeeper because Arsenal offer no firm confirmation that he starts in Gameweek 12.
Alexander Isak is a leading captaincy consideration away to Brighton, even with Newcastle’s difficult recent away record in this fixture.
Bruno Fernandes misses Manchester United training with a virus and remains a late call for Brentford.
Cody Gakpo misses Liverpool’s derby against Everton with a muscle problem, while James Tarkowski begins a three-match suspension.
Chelsea’s Moises Caicedo is available after a knock, but Joao Pedro and Reece James remain out.
Kaoru Mitoma is still unavailable for Brighton, while Matt O’Riley is a doubt after an ankle issue in midweek.
Tottenham lose Savio until after Christmas with a recurring hamstring injury, and Bergvall is ill.
Watch late illness updates at Bournemouth and Sunderland, where several players are affected or at risk.

items.title: FPL GW12 EXPERTS TEAM 🚀 430x Top 10k! 🚨 BEST GW12 TEAM!
items.headline: Calvert-Lewin is the leading Gameweek 12 captain as elite managers target short-term fixtures
items.summary:
Gameweek 12 presents an unusually open captaincy call, with 13 different players receiving expert support. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the clear leader, backed by 43% of experts, with De Kuiper a distant second on 13%. Calvert-Lewin’s home form and Leeds’ favourable fixture make him the preferred armband choice, while Isak, Jackson, Bruno Fernandes, Kevin De Bruyne, Haaland and several Brighton options also attract votes. The lack of consensus makes this a week to weigh individual squad structure and risk appetite rather than chase a supposedly obvious pick.

The biggest team-news issue is Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya. Reports suggest he may be close to returning, but the timescale remains uncertain ahead of Arsenal’s meeting with Manchester City. Managers with Raya are generally advised to hold if he is expected to miss only one match, particularly if they have a viable deputy, but to buy a replacement such as Trafford or Kinski if the absence looks longer. Verbruggen replaces Raya in the expert squad largely for budget reasons, although Kinski remains the most-owned goalkeeper and offers cover for Raya owners.

Defender Muheremovic is the standout transfer target. He averages more than 10 defensive contributions per 90 minutes and has reached the two-point defensive-contribution threshold in 64% of appearances, making him an appealing route into a favourable home fixture. De Kuiper, Van Hecke and Leeds defensive options are also prominent, while Vuskovic’s ownership continues to rise. The expert XI is Verbruggen; De Kuiper, Muheremovic and Van Hecke; Gross, Palmer, Rogers and Tavernier; then Calvert-Lewin, Haaland and Jackson.

Chip use is active in Gameweek 12. A Free Hit draft targets Coventry and Ipswich offensively while doubling on Brighton and Leeds defence, with Calvert-Lewin captained ahead of a front three also containing Jackson and Isak. The appeal is to exploit a short-term fixture window, avoid starting Arsenal assets against City and preserve transfers for the congested December schedule. Bench Boost managers are prioritising secure minutes, with one notable setup using Kinski, Van Hecke, Rogers and Alisson on the bench after a Gameweek 11 Wildcard.

Haaland is the main strategic fault line. Some managers bench or sell him to unlock Bruno Fernandes, Jackson, Calvert-Lewin and fixture-driven upgrades, especially with multiple free transfers available. Others retain him despite Manchester City’s form, citing his record of scoring in six of eight matches against Arsenal and the likelihood that he remains a leading captaincy option soon. The broader advice is not to sell reliable starters simply because returns have briefly dried up: December injuries, rotation and suspensions can quickly make depth and saved transfers valuable.
key_points: Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the leading Gameweek 12 captain, receiving 43% of expert backing in an exceptionally divided captaincy week.
Muheremovic is the top defender buy, combining a favourable fixture with a 64% hit rate for defensive-contribution points.
Raya owners can hold if he is likely to miss only one match, but Trafford or Kinski are the main replacement options if Arsenal confirm a longer absence.
The expert Gameweek 12 squad starts Verbruggen, De Kuiper, Muheremovic, Van Hecke, Gross, Palmer, Rogers, Tavernier, Calvert-Lewin, Haaland and Jackson.
Free Hit teams focus on short-term attacking targets against Coventry and Ipswich, alongside double Brighton and double Leeds defensive coverage.
Some managers sell Haaland for Bruno Fernandes and squad upgrades, but keeping him remains viable given his strong scoring record against Arsenal and future captaincy appeal.
Palmer is the second-most sold player, while Verts is among the most in-form midfielders with 35 points across the last four Gameweeks.
Managers are advised to protect players with strong minutes through the congested period rather than react too aggressively to a short run without returns.

items.title: 🚨 João Pedro update 🚨 Buy Kinsky? ✅ Sell Mbeumo? 🤔 FPL GW12 Final Thoughts 🔥
items.headline: Calvert-Lewin gets the armband as João Pedro becomes a sell ahead of Gameweek 12
items.summary:
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the preferred captain for Gameweek 12 at home to Coventry, in a week with no outstanding premium captaincy option. Pascal Groß narrowly ranks ahead of Brighton team-mate Diego Kiper because attackers are generally favoured over defenders, although Kiper’s clean-sheet potential and attacking role make him a viable high-upside alternative. Morgan Gibbs-White remains a good selection despite Chelsea having Moisés Caicedo available, while Cole Palmer is still playable because of his penalties and secure minutes, even if his form and underlying numbers make that judgement difficult to justify against a solid Forest defence.

João Pedro is ruled out for Gameweek 12 and has no confirmed return date for Chelsea’s home match against Crystal Palace in Gameweek 13. With Liverpool and Manchester City following, and several attractive forwards available, he is a sell for most managers unless they have a strong enough squad to bench him comfortably. A move to Calvert-Lewin is particularly appealing for managers with Erling Haaland plus Alexander Isak or Nicolas Jackson, as Pedro is blocking a valuable forward slot. Chelsea’s longer-term schedule improves again from Gameweek 16, but waiting indefinitely for Pedro’s fitness is an unnecessary risk.

Haaland is not essential away to Arsenal, and this is one of the clearer weeks to bench him if a squad has eight strong attackers or defenders with good fixtures. Selling him for Isak can unlock Bruno Fernandes and potentially Gabriel, creating a stronger spread of funds and a useful captaincy rotation. However, the move depends on trusting Isak’s fitness and workload through the congested schedule, plus Fernandes improving on modest returns despite decent underlying numbers. Haaland remains a strong captaincy option in Gameweeks 13, 15 and 16, so Gameweek 17 is presented as the more natural point for a major squad pivot if managers are not ready to sell now.

Diego Kiper remains worth buying at £5.6m despite his heavy ownership and recent price rises. He offers unusually strong attacking numbers for a defender, regular clean-sheet potential and largely secure minutes, even after playing 45 minutes in Europe. There is a case for waiting through tougher away trips to Bournemouth and Forest, but the risk is missing another haul and further price increases. In defence, Murmurovic is preferred long term if managers can bench him in difficult fixtures, while Jac may be better over the next four weeks for those planning a Free Hit in Gameweek 14. Harvey Barnes is worth holding rather than selling for Tavernier on one transfer: Tavernier has the superior immediate fixture but sits on four yellow cards, making a suspension disruptive during a busy period.

With four free transfers and £1.8m available, the likely move is McNair to Kinsky as goalkeeper cover for the doubtful David Raya, unless Arsenal provide a convincing positive update. The squad otherwise looks strong enough to avoid forcing Murmurovic in purely to bench Palmer, Rogers or Haaland. Preserving transfers is valuable before the Gameweek 13 midweek round, when minor injuries or rotation could quickly create problems. Calvert-Lewin remains captain, while an Inbeumo sale for Wirtz or Gibbs-White is more likely to be considered in Gameweek 13 if a Gameweek 14 Free Hit is confirmed.
key_points: Captain Calvert-Lewin at home to Coventry in Gameweek 12, with Groß and Kiper viable alternative captaincy options.
Sell João Pedro for most squads after confirmation he misses Gameweek 12 and has no clear Gameweek 13 return date.
Haaland is benchable away to Arsenal for managers with strong alternatives, but selling him requires confidence in Isak’s fitness and Bruno Fernandes’ output.
Kiper is still a buy at £5.6m because of his left-sided attacking role, clean-sheet potential and strong underlying numbers.
Palmer remains playable against Forest because of penalties and minutes, but Gibbs-White can reasonably be ranked ahead of him.
Hold Harvey Barnes if transfers are limited; Tavernier has immediate upside but is one booking from suspension.
For Free Hit 14 managers, Jac may edge Murmurovic over the next four gameweeks, while Murmurovic is preferred longer term if his tougher fixtures can be covered.
Kinsky is the likely goalkeeper transfer to cover Raya uncertainty, with the remaining transfers retained for Gameweek 13 rotation and injury news.

items.title: WIRTZ IN? 🔴 | Sam's FPL GW12 Transfer Tips
items.headline: Florian Wirtz emerges as a £7.4m midfield buy after back-to-back double-digit hauls
items.summary:
Florian Wirtz is the standout transfer target ahead of the next gameweek after producing 27 FPL points across Gameweeks 10 and 11. His 14-point return against Manchester United includes a goal, an assist, a clean sheet point and maximum bonus, leaving only Keane Lewis-Potter above him for the gameweek.

The underlying numbers support the recent returns rather than suggesting a fluke. Wirtz creates 10 chances against United, five of them big chances, and his 33 chances created for the season are the most of any player in FPL. Across the last seven gameweeks he records 48 points, with only three players scoring more, while his five assists in that spell cannot be bettered by any other player.

Wirtz is also central to Liverpool’s attack, involved in 34% of their chances through shots and chances created, more than any team-mate. That combination of creativity, involvement and recent output makes him a strong candidate to become the leading premium-style midfield option despite costing only £7.4m.

With many expensive midfielders underperforming and much of the value so far coming from cheaper names such as Pascal Groß, Jack Rudoni and Morgan Rogers, Wirtz offers a convincing route into a stronger price bracket without sacrificing budget. Buying him this week is endorsed, and pairing him with Alexander Isak is viewed as a sensible double-up strategy.
key_points: Florian Wirtz is the most transferred-in player for the upcoming gameweek after 13 and 14-point hauls in Gameweeks 10 and 11.
Wirtz scores, assists, keeps a clean sheet and earns three bonus points in Liverpool’s Gameweek 11 win over Manchester United.
He creates 10 chances against United, including five big chances, and leads all FPL players for chances created this season with 33.
Over the last seven gameweeks, Wirtz records 48 points and five assists, with only three players scoring more FPL points in that period.
Wirtz is involved in 34% of Liverpool’s chances this season, the highest share among Liverpool players.
At £7.4m, Wirtz is recommended as a value premium midfield purchase in a season of disappointing high-priced midfielders.
Doubling up on Wirtz and Alexander Isak is considered a strong squad-building move.

items.title: FPL GW12 Team Selection: My Raya Solution ⚠️ | Transfers & Captain
items.headline: Calvert-Lewin becomes Gameweek 12 captaincy target as Palmer exit funds Leeds move
items.summary:
Gameweek 12 presents a difficult FPL decision around David Raya, Cole Palmer and captaincy. Raya is rated roughly 50/50 to recover from his nerve-related issue in time for Arsenal’s match with Manchester City, with no indication of a serious injury. The preference is to hold him rather than spend a transfer on a goalkeeper likely to return quickly: even if Raya misses out, his expected return against City is modest and a saved transfer is valued at around three points. The calculus is helped by a planned Free Hit in Gameweek 13, which protects against a further absence. If stronger news rules Raya out, a switch to Leeds goalkeeper Trafford remains an alternative.

The main transfer priority is Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has home fixtures against Coventry in Gameweek 12 and Ipswich in Gameweek 14 either side of Leeds’ Gameweek 13 trip to Manchester City. Those fixtures make him both a strong short-term forward and a captaincy option, with Calvert-Lewin preferred over Bruno Fernandes, Isak and Nicolas Jackson for the armband in Gameweek 12. The intended move is Barry to Calvert-Lewin, funded most likely by selling Palmer for Florian Wirtz. Palmer’s underlying numbers remain poor, with no open-play goal since Gameweek 2 and only one penalty return since, while Wirtz combines strong recent form with elite creativity and offers funds for future moves.

Bruno Fernandes is retained and started because Brentford concede the league’s highest expected-goal volume to right wingers, matching his expected role on that flank. Pascal Gross also starts against a defensively vulnerable Newcastle, while Rogers stays despite limited recent output because he continues to deliver and has a history of outperforming his numbers. Jackson is favoured for Ipswich, but Barry is increasingly expendable: Liverpool look defensively strong and Barry’s coming schedule offers few fixtures worth starting him in. Sharda remains benched amid uncertain minutes, with no convincing cheap midfield replacement currently available.

The defensive core of Diper, Vuskovic and Muharovic is kept, supported by strong clean-sheet projections for Leeds and Brighton. Arsenal defenders are also considered playable against Manchester City despite the fixture. Haaland may be benched if Raya is confirmed fit, but he starts if Arsenal’s goalkeeper is absent because the replacement is seen as a meaningful defensive downgrade. Silva is a viable bench option ahead of one of Haaland, Palmer or Rogers. Looking ahead, the Gameweek 13 Free Hit draft leans towards double Liverpool defence, Spurs coverage, Palmer, Rogers, Gibbs-White, Rodoni and Haaland, prioritising talismanic players with secure minutes amid expected rotation.
key_points: Captain Dominic Calvert-Lewin in Gameweek 12, with his home match against Coventry offering the best blend of fixture, penalties and minutes security.
Hold David Raya unless reliable late news makes him unlikely to face Manchester City; Trafford is the contingency downgrade to fund Calvert-Lewin.
Sell Cole Palmer for Florian Wirtz to finance Barry to Calvert-Lewin, banking on Wirtz’s creative output and form while Palmer’s open-play threat remains low.
Start Bruno Fernandes against Brentford, who concede more xG to opposition right wingers than any other Premier League side.
Keep and play Gross against Newcastle, while retaining Rogers despite mediocre chance volume because of his ability to outperform expected returns.
Bench Sharda because his minutes are insecure, and avoid forcing a move to cheap midfield alternatives without reliable starts.
Consider benching Haaland only if Raya is confirmed fit; otherwise start him against a potentially weakened Arsenal goalkeeping situation.
Plan a Gameweek 13 Free Hit around double Liverpool defence and high-minutes attackers, then consider a Gameweek 15 defensive upgrade such as Muharovic to Virgil van Dijk.

items.title: SHOULD YOU SELL HAALAND?!❓| FPL GW12 Q&A WITH SAM + AZ | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Alexander Isak leads captaincy as Erling Haaland becomes a Gameweek 12 bench dilemma
items.summary:
Gameweek 12 presents an unusually open captaincy contest, with Alexander Isak the preferred pick for both panelists over Erling Haaland's trip to Arsenal. Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Kaoru Mitoma are also viewed as strong home-fixture options, while Nicolas Jackson and Liverpool's Florian Wirtz are viable alternatives. Haaland's poor form and Arsenal's defensive strength make him a credible captaincy fade, but not an automatic bench: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is a major doubt after appearing in a sling, and a weakened Arsenal back line could still give Haaland a route to returns.

The advice is to resist selling Haaland for hits. A proposed move of Haaland and Manzambi to Calvert-Lewin and Bruno Fernandes for a minus four is considered too risky, because it makes regaining Haaland difficult if he returns immediately. Managers determined to oppose Haaland are better served by a Free Hit rather than restructuring their permanent squad. Haaland may rank outside the very best forward picks this week, but he remains safer than benching him for a low-upside option such as Hull's Belloumi.

Cole Palmer is now a sell candidate, with Chelsea travelling to a Nottingham Forest side that continues to post strong defensive numbers despite poor recent results. Wirtz is preferred to Fernandes as a replacement: Liverpool are in form, Wirtz leads the league for assists over the last seven gameweeks and is also among the leading chance creators. Fernandes has penalties and Brentford have not kept an away clean sheet, but Manchester United remain too unpredictable to make him the priority. Moving Aston Villa's Manzambi to Wirtz is endorsed over spending a transfer on goalkeeper Edouard Mendy to Antonio Silva, particularly because Manzambi's uncertain starts and frequent early substitutions limit his appeal.

Managers without a playing goalkeeper should wait for Mikel Arteta's Raya update where possible, but replacing a non-playing backup such as Martin Dubravka with Kinsky is favoured over selling Raya immediately. That creates a usable goalkeeper rotation and avoids wasting a transfer if Raya's absence is brief. At the back, Bournemouth's Mahamoudovic is rated clearly above Leeds' James Justin because of stronger security of starts and longer-term upside. A Gameweek 14 Free Hit is the preferred chip plan, especially for managers lacking Leeds, Brighton, Tottenham or Liverpool coverage; it can also provide short-term access to Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo without committing to them long term.
key_points: Captain Alexander Isak ahead of Haaland, with Calvert-Lewin, Mitoma, Jackson and Florian Wirtz all credible Gameweek 12 alternatives.
Do not sell Haaland for a hit; a Free Hit is the cleaner route for managers who want to oppose him against Arsenal.
David Raya is a serious doubt after being seen in a sling, but there is no definitive Arsenal update before Arteta speaks.
Sell Cole Palmer if a route exists, with Wirtz preferred over Bruno Fernandes because of Liverpool's form and Wirtz's elite recent creativity.
Manzambi to Wirtz is a stronger transfer priority than a defensive reshuffle, given Manzambi's insecure minutes.
If Raya is your only active goalkeeper concern, upgrade the non-playing backup to Kinsky rather than immediately transferring Raya out.
Mahamoudovic is preferred to James Justin as the Leeds/Bournemouth defensive target due to better security and upside.
Gameweek 14 is the favoured Free Hit timing, particularly for squads short of Leeds, Brighton, Spurs and Liverpool players.

items.title: My Team Selection for Gameweek 12 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Calvert-Lewin is the locked-in captain as Raya cover tops Gameweek 24 plans
items.summary:
The priority for Gameweek 24 is solving the goalkeeper issue without selling David Raya. Raya is flagged and the current reserve goalkeeper, McNally, does not play, but the injury appears short term and Arsenal’s longer-term fixtures remain appealing. The preferred move is therefore McNally to Kinsky, funded by £1.8m in the bank, rather than moving on Raya prematurely.

At the back, Vuskovic and De Cuypere remain a defensive double-up after narrowly missing out on a clean sheet last week, with another favourable fixture ahead. De Cuypere is a captaincy temptation but is more likely to receive the vice-captaincy. Van Hecke is playable, although there is consideration of selling either Calafiori or Konsa for Moore-Removic. That transfer is not especially appealing, however, because a planned Free Hit in Gameweek 14 would mean Moore-Removic is likely to start only twice across the next six gameweeks.

Cole Palmer’s recent form is unconvincing, but holding is judged preferable to forcing a move to Florian Wirtz. Wirtz has Everton away and Sunderland at home over the next two gameweeks, while Palmer faces Nottingham Forest away and Crystal Palace at home, leaving little enough between the fixture runs to justify rolling the transfer. A Calafiori-to-Moore-Removic move could free funds for Palmer to Bruno Fernandes, but the planned Free Hit reduces the urgency. Morgan Rogers is also a hold, particularly with Crystal Palace at home next, while Bermo’s uncertain role as a number nine under Pochettino limits his longer-term appeal. Pascal Gross remains a strong pick.

Up front, Nicolas Jackson, Erling Haaland and Dominic Calvert-Lewin are all straightforward holds. Haaland can be benched by managers with stronger squads, but he starts here. Calvert-Lewin is the clear captaincy choice thanks to secure minutes, penalty duties and a good fixture. Fernandes would become an appealing high-risk differential captain if Palmer were sold, but that move is unlikely this week.
key_points: Transfer priority is McNally to Kinsky for goalkeeper cover, while keeping the short-term flagged Raya for Arsenal’s favourable longer-term schedule.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the preferred Gameweek 24 captain because he is nailed for minutes, takes penalties and has a decent fixture.
De Cuypere is the likely vice-captain after the defensive double-up with Vuskovic nearly delivered a clean sheet last week.
Van Hecke is fit to play, so selling Calafiori or Konsa for Moore-Removic is optional rather than urgent.
Moore-Removic is a short-term concern because a planned Free Hit in Gameweek 14 would limit his starts to roughly two in the next six gameweeks.
Palmer is held despite poor recent returns, with his fixtures close enough to Wirtz’s that rolling the transfer is preferred.
Palmer to Bruno Fernandes is affordable if Calafiori is sold for Moore-Removic, but it is less attractive with a Free Hit planned.
Jackson, Haaland and Calvert-Lewin are all holds, although Haaland is benchable for managers with greater squad depth.

items.title: MY FPL GW12 TEAM SELECTION! 💥 RAYA INJURED!
items.headline: Raya injury forces a goalkeeper dilemma as Kyper gets the captaincy against Newcastle
items.summary:
A 34-point Gameweek 11, featuring a third consecutive Erling Haaland captaincy blank, leaves the squad short of immediate fixes despite confidence in its longer-term structure. Summer arrivals Vuskovic and Jackson both disappoint, while Silva rewards selection over Barry with an eight-point clean sheet and DefCon return. Van Hecke adds six points, but late goals against Brighton wipe out a potentially decisive double clean sheet. Sharda’s surprise benching reinforces plans to sell him, although Raya’s injury now takes priority.

Raya misses Arsenal’s Champions League squad and Mikel Arteta suggests the goalkeeper could be unavailable for weeks, albeit not for months. With Bentley as the only reserve keeper, the preferred solution is to buy Kinsky if Raya is ruled out for Gameweek 12, then return to Raya when fit rather than spend two transfers selling and later rebuying him. Alisson and Trafford are the preferred direct Raya replacements if a longer absence is confirmed: Liverpool offer excellent fixtures but Alisson carries injury risk, while Trafford has strong home fixtures and bonus potential. The complication is Kinsky’s expected price rise and the need to act before Arteta’s Friday update.

The planned Gameweek 12 XI is Raya or a replacement behind Kyper, Van Hecke, Vuskovic and Silva; Sumo, Palmer, Rogers and Gross; plus Haaland and Jackson. Kyper receives the captaincy at home to Newcastle, provided he is rested in Europe, with Jackson vice-captain against leaky Ipswich. It is an aggressive call because it effectively creates triple Brighton defensive exposure, but Brighton have a 34% clean-sheet probability, second only to Leeds, and Newcastle have conceded the league’s second-most set-piece attempts. Kyper offers clean-sheet, attacking-return and bonus upside, while Vuskovic also benefits from set-piece weakness.

Haaland at Arsenal is the obvious captaincy fade, though he remains in the XI because he has six goals in eight league matches against Arsenal and has scored in four consecutive league meetings with Arteta’s side. Barry is considered but remains benched against Liverpool. Silva remains a standout defender after four eight-pointers in five Gameweeks and a 73% DefCon hit rate, while Van Hecke supplies aerial threat and bonus appeal despite weaker DefCon numbers. Gross is viewed as a set-and-forget midfield pick given Brighton’s 21.5 expected goals, second only to Manchester City, while Palmer could eventually make way for Bruno Fernandes or Morgan Gibbs-White if transfers become available.

The likely next attacking move is Sharda to Szoboszlai for Liverpool’s Gameweek 13 home match against Sunderland, funded by the Kinsky route and exploiting Liverpool’s strong fixture run. That move may be lost if price changes intervene, and Brighton’s trip to Bournemouth in Gameweek 13 could also create awkward exposure for managers holding multiple players from both sides.
key_points: Captain Kyper against Newcastle in Gameweek 12, with Jackson vice-captain against Ipswich; Haaland is a viable captaincy fade away to Arsenal.
Raya’s injury is the immediate transfer priority after he misses Arsenal’s Champions League squad and Arteta indicates a possible absence of weeks.
Kinsky is the preferred short-term Raya cover if Raya is out, preserving the option to return to Arsenal’s first-choice goalkeeper without using another transfer.
Alisson and Trafford are the preferred permanent Raya replacements if the injury proves longer term, with Liverpool fixtures favouring Alisson and bonus potential favouring Trafford.
Silva remains a strong hold after four eight-point returns in five Gameweeks and a 73% DefCon hit rate, while Brighton’s defensive outlook supports Kyper, Van Hecke and Vuskovic.
Newcastle’s vulnerability at set pieces boosts the appeal of Brighton defenders, having allowed the second-most set-play attempts in the league.
Sharda is a planned sale after a surprise benching, with Szoboszlai targeted for Liverpool’s Gameweek 13 home fixture against Sunderland.
Palmer is understandable to sell after recent blanks, but a Raya issue and earlier transfers leave insufficient free transfers for a midfield reshuffle.

items.title: It's time to buy a goalkeeper 🧤 My FPL Team for GW12 🔥
items.headline: Calvert-Lewin edges wide-open Gameweek 12 captaincy as Raya cover drives transfer plans
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 produces a second successive red arrow after a 35-point score, with only Pascal Gross, Morgan Rogers, Jan Paul van Hecke and Dominic Calvert-Lewin returning. The squad remains broadly sound despite blanks from Haaland, Cole Palmer and Arsenal’s defensive double-up, but the immediate problem is David Raya’s fitness: the Arsenal goalkeeper is flagged and backup McNally is unavailable on loan. With four free transfers and £1.8m in the bank, the likeliest move is McNally to Spurs goalkeeper Antonín Kinský, who covers possible Raya absences in Gameweeks 12 and 13 against Sunderland and Fulham. Raya is worth retaining if the injury is short term because Arsenal’s defence and fixtures improve significantly from Gameweek 16.

A Free Hit in Gameweek 14 is increasingly likely, shaping the reluctance to make aggressive defensive transfers. Leeds defender Miro Emenovic is attractive for Coventry at home in Gameweek 12 because clean sheets tend to bring bonus points, but buying him would mean benching van Hecke and only using Emenovic twice in the following six weeks due to difficult fixtures and the planned Free Hit. One of Riccardo Calafiori or Ezri Konsa could make way, with Calafiori’s Christmas rotation risk a concern, but the move is not yet compelling enough. Bournemouth defenders are also being avoided for now: Fulham away, Brighton at home and Arsenal away are not strong enough to justify buying before a Free Hit removes their Hull fixture in Gameweek 14.

Midfield transfers are being deferred despite real concerns. Palmer’s underlying numbers are poor for a near-£10m asset, while Bryan Mbeumo’s appeal weakens if he continues playing wide rather than as a central forward. However, Palmer faces Nottingham Forest before Crystal Palace in Gameweek 13, Mbeumo has reasonable short-term fixtures, and there is no pressing need for the funds. Florian Wirtz is a viable Palmer replacement, while Morgan Gibbs-White and Dominik Szoboszlai are alternative upgrades when Sangaré is eventually sold, but none demands action this week. Bruno Fernandes is tempting after a midweek brace and would be a major differential captaincy option, yet a Gameweek 14 Free Hit offers the chance to own and captain him for Coventry at home without committing to the transfer now.

Up front, Nicolas Jackson is held for his strong run through Gameweek 15, with João Pedro a possible switch in Gameweek 16. Haaland stays despite Arsenal away, his toughest fixture of the season; selling him for Alexander Isak is unnecessary when Haaland remains a preferred captain option in Gameweeks 13, 15 and 16, while Isak’s workload may become an issue. Calvert-Lewin starts and takes the captaincy against Coventry at home, helped by penalties and stronger home appeal than Jackson away to Ipswich. Gross and De Cuyper are viable differential captaincy alternatives, particularly if chasing a defender-led clean sheet, but Calvert-Lewin is the safer call.
key_points: McNally to Antonín Kinský is the most likely Gameweek 12 transfer, though Raya fitness news could still prevent an early move.
A Gameweek 14 Free Hit is the preferred chip plan and reduces the value of short-term defensive purchases.
Miro Emenovic is a strong Leeds option for Coventry at home, but he is not yet worth a transfer if it means benching van Hecke and using him rarely afterwards.
Calafiori is more expendable than Konsa because of likely rotation, especially during the congested Christmas schedule.
Palmer to Florian Wirtz and Mbeumo to Wirtz or Gibbs-White remain future options, but midfield changes are unlikely in Gameweek 12.
Bruno Fernandes is appealing as a differential, but the planned Free Hit in Gameweek 14 makes an immediate purchase less attractive.
Calvert-Lewin is the preferred captain for Coventry at home, ahead of Jackson, Haaland, Gross and De Cuyper.
Haaland remains a hold despite Arsenal away, while Jackson is retained until at least Gameweek 16 when João Pedro becomes a possible replacement.

items.title: FPL GW12 EXPERT Transfer Trends & Best Captain! 🧠 100 Experts Reveal Gameweek 12 Team Plans
items.headline: Calvert-Lewin becomes the standout Gameweek 12 captain as experts overhaul their squads
items.summary:
Gameweek 12 is a transfer-heavy round, with 54% of the 100 surveyed FPL experts making one move, 25% making two and only 13% rolling. Goalkeeper issues drive much of the activity: Raya is doubtful for Arsenal's match against Manchester City, although the injury is reportedly less serious than first feared. Rather than sell Raya outright, the preferred response is to upgrade a £4.0m reserve goalkeeper, giving managers cover if he misses out. Kinsky is the leading cheap backup target, while Trafford is the favoured direct Raya replacement.

Florian Wirtz is the most popular expert signing, attracting 27 transfers and rising from 3% to roughly 30% ownership. His appeal is strengthened by the Everton fixture, particularly with Tarkowski absent, and he displaces Morgan Gibbs-White from the expert template. Other prominent targets are Leeds goalkeeper Maherovic ahead of Coventry, Trafford, Calvert-Lewin and Isak, while Liverpool defenders Virgil van Dijk and Jarell Quansah also gain interest. The broad theme is to target Liverpool and Leeds, with Brighton assets remaining viable for managers who are not already at their three-player limit.

The highest-priority expert-backed switches are Gvardiol to Maherovic, Tarkowski to Maherovic and Schade to Wirtz. Hall to Maherovic, a £4.0m goalkeeper to Kinsky for Raya owners, Raya to Trafford, and Barry to Calvert-Lewin are viewed as strong but less urgent moves. Selling Palmer, Gibbs-White or Konsa is more of a luxury or funding decision: Palmer sales are especially linked to managers intending to use a Free Hit in Gameweek 13. The experts are notably cool on popular wider-market options Evanilson, Hill and Okafor, all of whom attract little meaningful expert support.

Captaincy is unusually open because Erling Haaland faces Arsenal away. Calvert-Lewin is the clear first choice, captained by 33% of all experts and 79% of those who own him. For managers without him, Isak and Bruno Fernandes offer the strongest alternative upside plays, with Nicolas Jackson and De Kuyper also in contention. Haaland remains owned by 97% of experts but receives only around 2% of captaincies, underlining the willingness to oppose him this week. Chip use is minimal in Gameweek 12, although many experts still retain their Free Hit and may deploy it in Gameweeks 13 to 15.
key_points: Calvert-Lewin is the leading Gameweek 12 captain, with 33% of experts backing him and 79% of his owners handing him the armband.
Raya is doubtful against Manchester City, so experts generally prefer upgrading a £4.0m backup goalkeeper to Kinsky rather than immediately selling Raya.
Trafford is the most popular direct replacement for Raya, while Kinsky is primarily bought as goalkeeper cover and is expected to rise from £4.4m.
Wirtz is the top transfer target ahead of Everton, with 27 expert purchases and a projected rise to about 30% expert ownership.
The most strongly endorsed transfers are Gvardiol or Tarkowski to Maherovic, and Schade to Wirtz.
Isak, Bruno Fernandes, Nicolas Jackson and De Kuyper are the main captaincy alternatives for managers without Calvert-Lewin.
Experts show little appetite for Evanilson, Hill and Okafor despite their popularity among the overall FPL player base.
Free Hit usage is scarce in Gameweek 12, but managers are increasingly positioning to use the chip in Gameweeks 13, 14 or 15.

items.title: RAYA INJURED 🤕⚠️ | THE FPL WATCHLIST GW12 WITH FPL HARRY 🔎 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Calvert-Lewin emerges as the Gameweek 12 captaincy play as Raya injury clouds Arsenal defence
items.summary:
David Raya’s injury is the main transfer complication ahead of Gameweek 12, with Arsenal giving no firm timescale beyond the possibility that he misses anywhere from Manchester City to a few weeks. The preferred approach is to keep Raya for Arsenal’s strong longer-term run, rather than sell a goalkeeper who should be wanted back quickly. Managers with a weak deputy are advised to upgrade that slot instead, with Guglielmo Vicario’s understudy Kinsky the value pick because he is cheapest and Spurs’ defensive numbers are strong. Verbruggen, Petrovic and Lucas Perri alternatives offer more save and bonus-point upside, but can block useful Brighton, Bournemouth or Leeds slots. Alisson is considered too injury-prone to be a safe Raya replacement.

Arsenal’s wider defensive appeal is reduced temporarily by Raya’s absence, William Saliba’s continued lack of minutes and Riccardo Calafiori’s rotation risk. Calafiori is unlikely to start every match in a dense sequence featuring Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham and Real Madrid, so owners need to be prepared to bench him rather than absorb one-point cameos. Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk has attractive fixtures but limited attacking data, making the cheaper Joe Gomez-style route more appealing if seeking Liverpool coverage. The immediate defensive transfer targets remain Leeds’ Jaka Bijol/Mahmoudovic-type options and Brighton’s Jan Paul van Hecke, with Bournemouth defenders also viable; clean sheets and defender bonus are increasingly deciding FPL ranks.

In midfield, Florian Wirtz is the leading premium replacement for Cole Palmer after back-to-back double-digit returns and a favourable Liverpool schedule against Everton, Sunderland, Chelsea and Leeds. However, his underlying figures are heavily boosted by recent matches against Crystal Palace and a 10-man Manchester United, so he is a calculated form pick rather than a risk-free move. Palmer’s lack of attacking output makes a sale defensible, especially for managers with two free transfers, although his upcoming run after Manchester City and Liverpool is excellent. Morgan Gibbs-White is a cheaper alternative with good fixtures, while Marcus Tavernier remains a reliable long-term Bournemouth option despite four yellow cards.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the standout forward transfer and captaincy candidate for Gameweek 12, with Coventry, Ipswich and Fulham at home in three of his next four. Leeds’ home form, his secure minutes and the captaincy potential against Coventry and Ipswich outweigh his poor away scoring record. He is preferred to Evanilson as a short-term buy, while Erling Haaland attracts little captaincy support away to Arsenal. Nicolas Jackson is also an option, but Aston Villa’s recent lack of goals limits confidence. Managers holding a Free Hit should consider its timing: Gameweek 14 is best for attacking Manchester United’s Coventry fixture, while Gameweek 15 may suit squads overloaded with Bournemouth at Arsenal, Chelsea at Manchester City and Leeds at Liverpool.
key_points: Keep David Raya if possible and upgrade the backup goalkeeper; Kinsky is the preferred low-cost deputy unless Arsenal confirm Raya’s quick return.
Avoid using a Free Hit solely to cover Raya’s absence, as better attacking opportunities exist in Gameweek 14 or Gameweek 15.
Calvert-Lewin is the priority forward buy and leading Gameweek 12 captain for Leeds’ home match against Coventry.
Florian Wirtz is the main Cole Palmer replacement, but his recent underlying numbers are inflated by exceptional games against Palace and 10-man Manchester United.
Selling Palmer for Wirtz is viable with spare transfers, but Palmer’s fixture run improves sharply after Chelsea face Manchester City and Liverpool.
Calafiori carries major rotation risk through Arsenal’s packed schedule and should be benched in predicted non-starts rather than relied upon every week.
Van Hecke, Leeds defenders and Bournemouth defenders remain strong value buys as defensive returns and bonus points continue to swing gameweeks.
Tavernier is a steady Bournemouth hold with six attacking returns in 11 matches, though his four yellow cards create suspension risk.
